## Findings
- claim-1: RWY Theorem 4.8 gives two integral generating families for \(J_v\): the right-adjoined and lower-adjoined families. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876]
- claim-2: RWY Conjecture 4.10 asserts that both families are minimal. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
- claim-3: St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), proves minimality only of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-4: The same paper’s Corollary 4.6 again formally concludes minimality only for the lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
- claim-5: Its Remark 4.7 identifies the right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) as conjugate to the proved family and says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments; it does not state a transposed theorem or corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
## Strategy
Compared RWY Theorem 4.8 and Conjecture 4.10 with St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, Corollary 4.6, and Remark 4.7. The requested bounded bibliographic target is established: the inspected 2024 full text formally proves only the lower-adjoined clause; it gives no formal theorem/corollary for the right-adjoined clause.

## Gaps
This is a bounded negative result for the inspected sources only, not for all literature. Any project proof of the right-adjoined clause is internal, not externally source-backed here.
